lesson_title: Find Any Street in Ten Seconds
hook_text: A city map has ten thousand streets. Here is how to find one of them in ten seconds.
clip_script: Step one: don't look at the map. Flip to the back, to the index. Every street is there in alphabetical order. Find your street. Next to it: a page number and a code, like D3. Step two: turn to the page. Look at the edges. Letters run across the top, numbers run down the side. Slide your finger across to D. Slide down to 3. Stop. Your street is in that one small square, out of hundreds. That is the whole trick: an alphabetical list plus a grid. Your phone's map app does exactly the same thing, only the search box is the index. But when the data runs out, the person who knows the grid still gets there.
visual_style: A whiteboard street guide flipping to the index, a finger tracing column D and row 3, a single square lighting up among hundreds, then a phone search bar morphing into the index page.
pacing: Countdown feel: step one, step two, done.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never get lost in a city again.
